sentences.text: If you steer only the front wheels of a long car, you get a wide circle.
But the long car swings so wide that its nose hits the wall.
A giant car takes about 12 meters to turn around, more than most driveways have.
So you add a motor that turns the rear wheels the opposite way, and the car pivots tighter.
At low speed the rear wheels turn against the front, so the car pivots and the turn shrinks from 12 to 10 meters.
But at highway speed those opposite rear wheels make the car twitchy, and the tail swings out.
So above 60 kilometers per hour, the rear wheels turn the same way as the front, and the car glides smoothly.
A Mercedes S-Class turns its rear wheels up to 10 degrees and cuts the turning circle by up to about 2 meters.
The GMC Hummer EV points all four wheels the same way at low speed, and the truck slides diagonally at a modest angle.
But if the rear motor jams with the wheels turned, the car veers sideways.
So a computer watches both axles and straightens the rear wheels the instant anything fails.
And four-wheel steering is not four-wheel drive, because spinning wheels are a different idea.
Steering only points the wheels, and which wheels push the car is a separate job.
Add a speed sensor, the body panels and headlights.
Congratulations, you have built a car with four-wheel steering.
